title: Keyboard Manager: Remapped Copilot key (F23) not recognized in Citrix Workspace session

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a concrete host-versus-Citrix comparison, exact key mapping, Citrix version, Windows build, and a second remapping tool that fails in the same native session. The next discriminator is maintainer-side verification of Citrix full-screen keyboard forwarding, not another generic log request.
evidence: The live issue body says Win+Shift+F23 remapped to Right Ctrl works locally but is ignored in Citrix Workspace 25.8.10.36 in the virtual desktop.
The reporter says the behavior changes when Citrix TransparentKeyPassthrough is set to Local, but that breaks local Alt+Tab.

On 2026-09-07 the reporter said a separate Copilot-key remapper also works locally but fails in the same Citrix session; the linked comment is https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/44650#issuecomment-5572801150.
The latest discussion comment hypothesizes a Citrix low-level input limitation but does not establish the cause: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/44650#issuecomment-5574514004.
A related open Copilot-key report, #50946, contains a different local Keyboard Manager initialization failure and does not establish a fix for this Citrix-only behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact host/Citrix comparison on a current supported build and trace which side receives the remapped key before proposing a code change.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-side compatibility change is possible but not yet justified. The parallel failure of another remapper suggests that Citrix full-screen input forwarding may be involved; this remains a hypothesis, not a confirmed PowerToys root cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate keyboard remapping across Citrix full-screen input forwarding
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Citrix's native full-screen keyboard path may not forward or accept the injected remapped key sequence in the same way as local applications; the issue does not yet prove whether PowerToys or Citrix owns the failure.
plan: Reproduce on the reported LG Gram/Citrix setup with the Copilot key mapped from Win+Shift+F23 to Right Ctrl; compare a local text editor, Citrix windowed mode, and Citrix full-screen mode.
Compare Citrix's reported TransparentKeyPassthrough settings and determine whether the remapped input reaches the host hook or the remote session.

Trace the Keyboard Manager low-level hook and injected-input path only if the failure differs from the other remapper; make a code change only if a PowerToys-owned interception defect is demonstrated.
Add a focused regression check for the proven host/Citrix input path, or document that the limitation is controlled by Citrix if the same input fails before PowerToys-specific handling.
verification: On a current supported PowerToys build, verify the remapping in a local editor, Citrix windowed session, and Citrix full-screen session.
Confirm Alt+Tab remains local and behaves as expected under the tested passthrough setting.

confidence.rationale: The issue is specific and reproducible, but the same failure in another remapper makes the owning component uncertain.

issue_context.summary: A Copilot-key remap works on the reporter's LG Gram locally but fails in a native Citrix desktop; browser-based Citrix succeeds, and a passthrough workaround changes which side receives system shortcuts.
known_information: The report identifies PowerToys 0.96.1, Windows 11 build 26200.7171, Citrix Workspace 25.8.10.36, and an LG Gram 2025.
The reporter maps the Copilot key, observed as Win (Left)+Shift (Left)+F23, to Right Ctrl and says it works in a local editor.
The reporter says the native Citrix session ignores the mapping, including in full-screen, while Citrix for HTML5 in Edge works.
The reporter says TransparentKeyPassthrough=Local changes the result but causes Alt+Tab to switch local windows instead of remote windows.
The reporter tried another Copilot-key remapper and observed the same Citrix failure.
The latest upstream activity is 2026-10-11T16:49:05Z; the latest public comment is 2026-09-07T18:39:04Z.
inferences: The native Citrix keyboard-forwarding path may be responsible, but the parallel failure in another remapper is suggestive rather than proof.
The distinct HTML5 result indicates that the failure is not simply that the physical Copilot key is unrecognized by every application.
issue_context.analysis: The issue already contains enough controlled comparisons to avoid asking for generic logs. A maintainer test can distinguish a PowerToys hook/injection defect from Citrix's full-screen input policy and avoids proposing unsupported behavior changes.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body and all six public comments; the final comment proposes a low-level Citrix limitation but supplies no confirming trace.
Checked the linked, open issue #50946; its reported local Keyboard Manager initialization failure is not evidence that the Citrix-specific path is fixed.

Checked the owning Keyboard Manager event-handler path in src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp; the existing low-level hook and app-specific handling do not establish Citrix compatibility.

reproduce.version_requirement: Use a current supported PowerToys build; compare with the reported 0.96.1 behavior if available.
prerequisites: A laptop with a dedicated Copilot key recognized as Win+Shift+F23.
Citrix Workspace native client and a remote desktop session.
A local text editor and a remote application that can distinguish Right Ctrl.
steps: Map Win (Left)+Shift (Left)+F23 to Right Ctrl in Keyboard Manager.
Verify the mapping in a local text editor.
Open the same remote desktop in Citrix windowed mode and test the key.
Switch Citrix to full-screen mode and test the key again.
If permitted, compare Citrix TransparentKeyPassthrough settings and record whether Alt+Tab remains local or is forwarded remotely.
reproduce.expected: The same remapped Right Ctrl input is received in the local and Citrix contexts, unless Citrix explicitly owns or suppresses that input path.

actions.label: Approve focused compatibility investigation
actions.note: The proposed plan is a low-confidence hypothesis pending maintainer reproduction.
